report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/kairos/drafts.py chunk 1 of 1; enumerated all docstring/comment claims, found two broken claims (unsafe save_draft path, non-atomic status write), plus minor observations.
risks: save_draft | high | Draft path is built from user-controlled objective without safe_path; a crafted objective can select an arbitrary file under runs/drafts (e.g. via ../ or absolute path) and overwrite it. | Confirm whether save_draft is reachable with untrusted objective; if so, use _safe_path or sanitize.

set_status | medium | Status write is not atomic (read-modify-write with write_text); concurrent updates can lose the status_changed field or interleave. | Check if set_status can be called concurrently; if so, use atomic replace.
apply_payload | low | Marks draft as applied even if set_status fails (e.g. race); packet is returned anyway. | Verify whether set_status failure should abort the handoff.
list_drafts | low | Skips unreadable drafts silently; could hide corruption. | Confirm whether silent skip is intended.
get_draft | low | Returns raw JSON without validating schema; consumers may assume fields exist. | Check if downstream code handles missing keys.

handoff.purpose: Persist advisory drafts to runs/drafts; provide list/get/delete/status/apply operations with a path-traversal guard.

symbols.name: ROOT
symbols.note: Repository root computed as parents[2] of this file; used for DRAFT_DIR.

symbols.name: _SLUG_RE
symbols.note: Regex to replace non-alphanumeric characters in slugs.

symbols.name: _ID_RE
symbols.note: Regex to validate draft ids as plain stems (1-120 alnum, dot, underscore, hyphen).

symbols.name: _slug
symbols.note: Converts text to a safe slug: lowercases, replaces non-alphanumeric runs with '-', strips leading/trailing '-', truncates to max_len, defaults to 'draft'.

symbols.name: _safe_path
symbols.note: Returns a Path only if draft_id matches _ID_RE and the resolved path stays inside DRAFT_DIR; otherwise None.

symbols.name: save_draft
symbols.note: Writes a draft JSON to DRAFT_DIR with a timestamp-slug filename, avoiding overwrite by appending -n. Returns the path.

symbols.name: list_drafts
symbols.note: Reads all *.json in DRAFT_DIR, returns newest-first summaries; skips unreadable files.

symbols.name: get_draft
symbols.note: Reads and returns a draft dict if the id is safe and the file exists; None otherwise.

symbols.name: delete_draft
symbols.note: Deletes a draft file if the id is safe and the file exists; returns True on success.

symbols.name: set_status
symbols.note: Updates a draft's status and adds status_changed timestamp; raises ValueError on invalid status; returns updated draft or None.

symbols.name: apply_payload
symbols.note: Builds a review packet from a draft and marks it 'applied' via set_status; returns the packet or None.

claims.text: Here every accepted advisory report is persisted to ``runs/drafts/<ts>-<slug>.json`` so it can be listed, reviewed, applied, and cleaned up later
claims.why: save_draft writes to DRAFT_DIR with a ts-slug filename; list_drafts, get_draft, delete_draft, apply_payload provide the listed operations.

claims.text: Apply is deliberately NOT automated: a draft is a proposal, and the safety model says a free model may propose but never merge.
claims.why: apply_payload only returns a packet and calls set_status; no filesystem writes to target repo occur in this module.

claims.text: This module moved one package level deeper. Runtime state remains at the repository root for backward compatibility with every existing draft.
claims.why: ROOT is computed as parents[2] from this file, which is two levels up (kairos -> daedalus -> root), and DRAFT_DIR is ROOT/runs/drafts.

claims.text: Closes the path-traversal gap Minos would have flagged.
claims.why: _safe_path validates the id with a strict regex and verifies the resolved path is inside DRAFT_DIR.

claims.text: Resolve a draft id to its file ONLY if the id is a plain stem that stays inside DRAFT_DIR. Returns None for anything suspicious (``..``, separators, absolute paths, symlink escapes).
claims.why: The regex rejects separators and '..'; resolution and relative_to check prevent symlink escapes.

claims.text: Write one accepted advisory report to the drafts store; returns the path.
claims.why: Function writes a JSON file and returns the Path.

claims.text: never overwrite an existing draft from the same second
claims.why: The while loop checks path.exists() and appends -n until a non-existing path is found.

claims.text: Newest-first summaries of every stored draft.
claims.why: Files are sorted with reverse=True, so newest filenames (timestamp-based) come first.

claims.text: Transition a draft's lifecycle. Returns the updated draft, or None if the id is unknown; raises ValueError on an invalid status.
claims.why: Invalid status raises ValueError; unknown id returns None; otherwise returns the updated dict.

claims.text: This does NOT touch the filesystem of the target repo -- 'applied' only marks the proposal as handled (a free model may propose, never merge; the actual edit is a human / Claude action).
claims.why: The function only writes to DRAFT_DIR; no repo paths are used.
Setting the same status twice produces the same result (status_changed updates, but the state is consistent).

claims.text: The review packet a human / the Claude lane needs to ACTUALLY apply a draft: the objective, the target paths, and the proposal text. Marks the draft 'applied' (handled) but performs no write itself -- returning the packet IS the handoff.
claims.why: The packet contains objective, paths, proposal (from report.summary), and the function calls set_status; no repo writes occur.

claims.text: None if the id is unknown.
claims.why: get_draft returns None for unknown ids, and apply_payload returns None in that case.

claims.text: A draft id is our own timestamp-slug stem. It arrives from the CLI and from URL path segments (/api/drafts/<id>/apply), so it MUST NOT be trusted into a filesystem path -- reject anything that isn't a plain stem (no separators, no traversal).
claims.why: _ID_RE allows only alphanumerics, dot, underscore, hyphen; _safe_path enforces containment.

claims.text: Closes the path-traversal gap Minos would have flagged.
claims.why: The _safe_path check prevents traversal via symlink and '..'.

claims.text: Runtime state remains at the repository root for backward compatibility with every existing draft.
claims.why: DRAFT_DIR is defined as ROOT/runs/drafts, which is the repository root.

observations.what: save_draft constructs the draft file path directly from user-controlled objective without using _safe_path or sanitizing the slug for path separators. Although _slug replaces non-alphanumeric characters, it does not strip path separators like '/' or '\'; on POSIX, a slash in the slug would create a subdirectory, and on Windows a backslash could do the same. This can lead to writing outside DRAFT_DIR (e.g., objective containing '../' would result in a path like runs/drafts/../filename.json, which resolves outside DRAFT_DIR).

set_status performs a non-atomic read-modify-write: it reads the JSON, mutates the dict, and writes with write_text. If two processes call set_status concurrently, one can overwrite the other's changes (lost update). The docstring claims idempotency, but not atomicity.

apply_payload calls set_status but ignores its return value. If set_status fails (e.g., the file was deleted between get_draft and set_status), the draft is not marked applied, yet the packet is still returned. The docstring says it marks the draft applied; this can silently fail.
list_drafts silently skips files that fail to parse or read. This could hide corrupted drafts or permission issues.

get_draft returns the raw JSON dict without any schema validation. Downstream consumers might assume fields like 'report' exist; a malformed draft could cause KeyError in apply_payload (though it uses .get()).
